clue.text: Edward took in kinswoman when goaded

indicators.note: took in means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: Ted is a short form of the name Edward
an aunt is a female relative

explanation.surface: Edward's relative came to stay, and the visit got under his skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunting someone means provoking or needling them, so goaded is a synonym.

clue.text: A little European (frog, perhaps?)

parts.note: a tad means a little bit
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A small Continental creature, possibly a frog.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval stage of an amphibian such as a frog, so it is a frog in the making.

clue.text: With no ties, and heading nowhere?

definitions.meaning: loose, not fastened or tied up
something bound for somewhere is heading there, so one not so bound has no destination

explanation.definitionFit: The word means free from fastenings and, read as not bound for anywhere, without a destination.

clue.text: Shallow cups for boozers — or vast stein!

indicators.note: boozers suggest drunken rearrangement of the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Drinking vessels for drunks, or else one enormous beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: A tastevin is the small silver saucer a wine taster or sommelier uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastevins are small shallow silver cups used by wine tasters.

clue.text: The merit of French free verse

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: free suggests the letters of the word verse are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on the worth of French free verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to earn or be worthy of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Irritate worker by getting amorous

parts.note: to gall is to vex or irritate
a worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: Someone annoys a colleague by flirting with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Gallant here is stressed on the second syllable: attentive to women, courtly in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant man is chivalrous and attentive in courtship, close to amorous.

clue.text: It is usually difficult to eat

definitions.text: It is usually difficult to eat

parts.words: It is usually difficult to eat
parts.note: the clue describes the tough, chewy tissue found in cheap meat

explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is tough cartilage in meat that resists chewing.

clue.text: A girl with nothing is a catch?

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A penniless young woman is still a good match.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is thrown to capture cattle, so it is a device for catching.

clue.text: Stirs up a row, says audition is needed

indicators.note: the words tell the solver the phrase must be listened to when spoken

parts.note: the phrase a row, says spoken quickly gives the sound needed

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out, and someone insists on a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up feelings is to excite or rouse them.

clue.text: Very French to get chaps into a kind of delirium!

indicators.note: into means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: très is French for very
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Getting the lads into the French style sends them into a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium tremens is the shaking delirium of alcohol withdrawal, so this is the word naming that kind.

clue.text: Lowers sea-bed's alignment

indicators.note: alignment suggests the letters of the phrase are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Something drags down the way the ocean floor is arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive's S counts here: SEABEDS has the seven letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is to reduce in value or quality, a synonym of lowers.

clue.text: Awaiting at the warehouse

definitions.meaning: goods kept in a store or depot are literally in the store

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both pending or about to happen and physically held in a storehouse.

clue.text: Overrule, to avoid mistake, plan for part of plant

indicators.note: to avoid means the named letters are kept out of the word before it

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: An instruction to correct a botanist's error before it spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking E, R, R out of OVERRULE leaves the five letters; the definition reads the ovule as the plant's blueprint for a seed.
explanation.definitionFit: In a flowering plant the ovule is the structure that develops into the seed, so it is the plan for that part.

clue.text: Snub old-fashioned American with vacant smile

parts.note: retro means in an old-fashioned style

indicators.note: vacant means the word smile is emptied of its inside, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone cold-shoulders a fusty American wearing a blank grin.
explanation.walkthrough: Snub is the adjective, as in a snub nose; retroussé describes a nose turned up at the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub nose is short and turned up, which is what a retroussé nose is.

clue.text: In the position to finally know!

parts.note: the end is what comes finally
being wise to something means knowing about it

explanation.surface: An exclamation about finally being in the know.
explanation.definitionFit: Endwise describes the way something is placed, with its end forward or upright, so it names a position.

clue.text: Shows up former attitudes

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an attitude can be a physical pose, as a model strikes

explanation.surface: A model displays the postures she used to adopt.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone up is to reveal their faults, which is to unmask them.

clue.text: Primary cause of royal taking one poet laureate

indicators.note: taking means the first piece holds the others

parts.note: a prince is a royal
I is the Roman numeral one
PL is the abbreviation for poet laureate

explanation.surface: The original reason a prince hired a court poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle in the old sense is a fundamental source or origin, a first cause.

clue.text: Fortunate, like actor Brian?

definitions.meaning: Brian ... is a booming British actor, so anyone sharing his surname fits

explanation.definitionFit: The word means lucky, and it is also the surname of the actor Brian Blessed.

clue.text: Cover-up on featureless extra-terrestrial

parts.note: blank means empty, without features

explanation.surface: A conspiracy to hide a faceless alien.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket is a bed covering, something that covers you up.

clue.text: Does he crack on with his studies?

definitions.text: Does he crack on with his studies?

parts.words: Does he crack on with his studies?
parts.note: to crack on is to press ahead, but cracking also suggests a shell, so the clue pictures an academic whose head is a breakable ovoid

explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is a studious intellectual, jokingly with a fragile, egg-shaped head.

clue.text: Condescended to allow Gide out with little Edwin

indicators.note: out suggests the name Gide is put out of order

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edwin

explanation.surface: Someone graciously lets the French novelist Gide leave with young Edwin.
explanation.walkthrough: André Gide is a French novelist, here only a name to be jumbled; 'out' is the anagram signal on his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something, which is to condescend.

clue.text: He might produce an engraving for the queen

parts.note: an engraving is a kind of print
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's monogram

explanation.surface: An engraver makes a picture to present to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns out books or pictures on a press is a printer, a person who might produce something.

clue.text: Praise for braid worn by aristocratic daughter

indicators.note: worn by means the inner pieces sit inside the braid like a garment around them

parts.note: a plait is a braid
U is the British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A noble girl in a plait is complimented.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of approval or applause.

clue.text: Berets used to carry beer and Mexican food

indicators.note: the hats are used to carry, so they hold the other piece inside

parts.note: tams are tam-o'-shanters, beret-like Scottish caps
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Hats are pressed into service carrying drink and snacks south of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamales are a Mexican dish of steamed corn dough with a filling.

clue.text: Withdraws and dresses again

definitions.meaning: goes away, retreats or leaves work for good
to re-tire in the old sense is to attire anew

explanation.definitionFit: The word means leaves or retreats, and read as re-tire it means puts clothes on once more.

clue.text: Old silver found in a south American country

parts.note: argent is the old and heraldic word for silver
taken as written

explanation.surface: Antique silverware turns up in a Latin American nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in southern South America.

clue.text: Nosy?

parts.note: nosy usually means prying, but read literally it describes what relates to the nose

explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, a literal sense of nosy.

clue.text: Shooting star will arrive on time

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: A promise that the meteor will appear punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is a celestial body that streaks across the sky, loosely called a shooting star.

clue.text: Ship's outer shell's on an inner shell

parts.note: the keel is the backbone along a ship's bottom, its outer structure
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a hull laid over another hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A keelson is the timber or girder fixed inside a ship along the keel, an inner structure.

clue.text: Physicist who undoubtedly had an effect

definitions.text: Physicist who undoubtedly had an effect

parts.words: Physicist who undoubtedly had an effect
parts.note: the change in pitch of a passing siren is named after an Austrian physicist, so he literally has an effect

explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian physicist Christian Doppler gave his name to the effect of motion on wave frequency.

clue.text: Walked unsteadily on one's own for a day, under guidance

parts.note: on your tod is British slang for alone, from rhyming slang Tod Sloan
D is the abbreviation for day
led means guided

explanation.surface: Someone went off alone for a day, but with a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: On one's tod is British slang for alone, from rhyming slang on a jockey's name, Tod Sloan.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk with short, tottering steps like a small child.

clue.text: Ship seen among trees, negotiating locks

indicators.note: among means one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation for a ship

explanation.surface: A vessel spotted between the trees as it passes through canal locks.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks are not on a canal but of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks and tresses are both long strands of hair.
